paragraphs: The GLC300d has been part of the GLC-Class range since the model launched in 2015. Early X253-generation cars (roughly 2015 to 2018) use the OM651 — a 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel shared with the C-Class family of that era. From around 2018, the GLC300d switched to the OM654, a newer 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel that continues into the current X254 generation. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the known wear pattern and the rebuild specifics differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every GLC300D on the road.

cards.body: A 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to early GLC300d models from 2015 to around 2018 (X253 generation). Known for injector seal leaks and timing chain wear — see the callout above. We replace injector seals, timing chain components and gaskets as standard on every OM651 rebuild.

A 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted from around 2018 onwards, continuing into the current X254 generation. A newer design that doesn't share the earlier engine's injector seal and timing chain pattern. We service it to the same standard as our other GLC300d rebuilds.

compatibility.intro: Because the GLC300d spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an OM651 part will work on an OM654 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic GLC-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
